To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
An attacker does not need to execute JavaScript to steal information from a well-secured website.

(1) an attacker can abuse CSS and related Web features in order to perform scriptless attacks, (2) these attacks can leak sensitive information from well-protected websites and (3) a mitigation technique against this type of attacks is to prevent the use of CSS and related features for a given website.
• The use of scripting languages is not a requirement for an attacker to perform information leakage attacks against websites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can an attacker steal the pie without touching its sill?
a new class of attacks, scriptless attacks.
the question whether an adversary can steal the pie without touching its sill.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attack surface is not only reduced by preventing JavaScript execution, but that it is also not eliminated.
an attacker can steal the pie without touching a single line of script code.
an attacker should not rely solely on XSS attacks, but should consider other techniques to perform attacks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
an attacker can still steal the pie without touching its sills.
a lot of effort has been put into mitigating the impact of XSS attacks, and that the security community has been successful in this regard.
the attack surface of the Web is much bigger than it appears at first sight.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a website can no longer assume that it is loaded in the same browser tab as its parent website, and therefore needs to be prepared to deal with this situation.
a website can be attacked without executing scripting code, which is an important observation for the security community and the Web developers.
a website owner needs to be aware of the fact that a user might not be using a browser with JavaScript enabled and still be able to perform certain kinds of attacks.
